notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. 64-year-old female admitted for upper GI bleed. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.55, creatinine 0.72-0.73, hemoglobin 10.9-12.9, platelets 210-216, sodium 140, wbc 6.4-7.1; vitals dbp 76-81, heart_rate 81-84, map 89-94, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 13-15, sbp 115-121, spo2 97-98, temp 36.7-36.9
Day 0 orders/meds/results: EGD: bleeding duodenal ulcer, treated with endoscopic clips; Pantoprazole 80 mg IV
Assessment and plan: Upper GI bleed. Hypertension.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 0.71-0.76, hemoglobin 10-10.8, platelets 206-210, sodium 139-140, wbc 6.7-7.1; vitals dbp 77-81, heart_rate 81-86, map 90-93, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 13-15, sbp 115-121, spo2 97-98, temp 36.7-36.9
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Transfuse 1 unit packed red blood cells
Assessment and plan: Upper GI bleed. Hypertension. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 64-year-old female, length of stay 3 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Upper GI bleed. Hypertension. Follow up with primary care in one week. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed.
